profiles.meeting_scenario: The team is troubleshooting a bug in a VS Code extension for probabilistic programming that provides online, interactive debugging of Bayesian inference runs. Over the last week, several internal users reported that after making small edits to a Bayesian model, the debugger sometimes shows a green 'converged' badge while the posterior plots and divergence markers still reflect an earlier run, especially in the Eight Schools sample project. The meeting is a 30-minute troubleshooting session between the inference runtime owner and the IDE integration owner to align on the likely root cause and decide what patch to ship in the next internal build. The agenda is to compare observed symptoms, identify whether the issue is in state reuse, event triggering, or diagnostics rendering, and agree on a narrowly scoped fix. The expected outcome is a shared plan for one corrective change and a validation approach for confirming the issue is resolved.

members.name: Leah Kim
members.expertise: MCMC implementations, stateful inference execution, sampler checkpointing, posterior diagnostics
members.background: Leah built the runtime layer that supports warm-started inference and incremental recomputation for the probabilistic programming debugger, and she previously worked on adaptive HMC systems in a research tooling team.
members.private_state: She wants to avoid disabling warm-starting because it is a flagship capability of the tool, and she is concerned that the bug will be blamed on the runtime even though she suspects the IDE layer is reusing UI artifacts incorrectly.
hidden_assumptions: When people say an inference run 'continues online,' they mean a resumed execution of the same chain state after a small model edit rather than a fresh short rerun.
The 'Eight Schools repro' refers to the internal NumPyro-based benchmark project under examples/eight_schools_incremental with a fixed seed and checkpointing enabled.

A run is effectively 'fixed' if the resumed chain's diagnostics are internally consistent and the convergence badge matches the current chain state, even if the user must trigger one more edit-save cycle to refresh plots.
Resuming 'from the last checkpoint' naturally includes sampler state and adaptation buffers, but not frontend-rendered plot caches or notebook-side transformed data artifacts.

members.name: Arjun Patel
members.expertise: IDE extensions, editor event pipelines, reactive UI state, developer experience instrumentation
members.background: Arjun owns the VS Code extension and the interactive diagnostics panel, with a background in language tooling and live programming interfaces rather than Bayesian computation itself.
members.private_state: He wants a fix that reduces user confusion quickly for the next internal study, and he is worried that if they frame the issue as runtime-specific they will miss a broader editor-state bug affecting multiple examples.
hidden_assumptions: When people say an inference run 'continues online,' they mean the IDE automatically launches a fresh lightweight rerun on every save so the UI always reflects the latest text buffer.
The 'Eight Schools repro' refers to the default PyMC-based sample workspace bundled with the extension, which autogenerates a new seed unless the user pins one.
A run is 'fixed' only if a typical user can trust that the posterior panels and badges correspond to the latest code immediately after save, without manually resetting or re-running anything.

Resuming 'from the last checkpoint' includes whatever the user experiences as prior context in the IDE: sampler state, cached diagnostics, transformed-data previews, and plot layers that should all move together.
If the convergence badge flips before the charts update, the problem is probably stale UI subscriptions rather than a valid partial runtime state.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss whether the issue appears during an 'online rerun' or 'live rerun' after an edit.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a warm-started continuation of an existing inference session that reuses chain state after a small code change.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a new lightweight rerun automatically started by the editor after each save, regardless of prior chain state.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In this product, both fresh reruns and resumed runs are marketed as 'online' and happen immediately after edits, so the phrase feels standard and not worth unpacking.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'Eight Schools' reproduction case they mean
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the Eight Schools sample' and 'the repro project' as if it is one shared case.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the internal NumPyro example with checkpoint reuse, fixed seed 13, and a local dev flag that preserves adaptation state.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the bundled PyMC sample workspace opened by study participants, with auto-seeding and no explicit checkpoint flag exposed in the UI.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The sample has the same model name, similar screenshots, and is commonly used in demos, so each assumes the other is referring to the same artifact.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the issue being 'fixed'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say they want the convergence status and diagnostics to be 'correct' after the patch.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks 'correct' means the backend's current chain state, divergence count, and convergence badge are internally consistent for the active resumed run.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks 'correct' means the entire user-facing diagnostics view, including plots and summaries, visibly corresponds to the latest saved code with no misleading stale elements.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are discussing correctness of diagnostics in good faith, and neither expects a distinction between backend consistency and fully synchronized user-visible state to matter at this level of troubleshooting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to inspect what happens when the system 'resumes from the last checkpoint.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes sampler position, mass matrix, adaptation buffers, and the serialized runtime execution state only.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes all user-visible persisted context tied to that run, including chart data caches, transformed-observation previews, and diagnostics panel subscriptions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Checkpointing is discussed as one coherent feature in the product, so the backend/frontend boundary inside that phrase stays invisible during normal collaboration.

turns.inner_thought: What I keep hearing is that after a tiny model edit, the resumed NumPyro Eight Schools benchmark under examples/eight_schools_incremental comes back with a green convergence badge while the posterior plots and divergence markers still look like the pre-edit run. In my head that's an online rerun of the same warm-started chain, not a brand-new execution. If the backend chain state is coherent, I don't want this framed as 'runtime is broken' just because the IDE is lagging on refresh. Also, for me, 'correct' means the resumed chain's diagnostics line up with the active state, even if the plots need one more UI cycle.
turns.utterance: I can kick us off. The symptom I think we're chasing is that during an online rerun after a small edit, the convergence badge goes green, but the posterior panels and divergence markers still look like the earlier state in the Eight Schools sample. So the question for me is why the status looks correct before the rest of the diagnostics do.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, that's basically what I've seen in the bundled PyMC sample workspace the study folks use. In my mind an online rerun is the editor auto-starting a fresh lightweight rerun on save so the UI always matches the latest buffer. If the badge flips and the panels are stale right after save, that's a live rerun pipeline problem, likely subscriptions or cached panel state. A fix only counts if the visible diagnostics are trustworthy immediately, not just eventually.
turns.utterance: Yeah, that matches what I've been seeing in the sample workspace too. On the live rerun path, right after save, the panel can look stale even though the status has already updated. From the extension side, that's exactly the kind of thing users read as the diagnostics not being correct.

turns.inner_thought: In my repro, the restored chain state, divergence count, and convergence summary are internally consistent after checkpoint restore. That makes me suspect the handoff boundary: runtime restores sampler position, mass matrix, and adaptation buffers, then emits convergence, but the frontend may still be showing old rendered artifacts. 'Resume from the last checkpoint' to me is runtime serialization, not plot caches or notebook transforms.
turns.utterance: What's making me look a bit away from the sampler itself is that in my reproduction the chain state and divergence counts line up. So my first instinct is to inspect what exactly is being carried forward when the system resumes from the last checkpoint, because the status path looks cleaner than the diagnostics rendering path.

turns.inner_thought: From the user's perspective, resume from checkpoint is one thing: whatever context they had before should advance together—status badge, charts, transformed previews, subscriptions, all of it. If some of that moves and some doesn't, users don't care whether the backend is internally coherent. They'll assume the tool is lying. I want to avoid a runtime-only narrative if the real issue is our broader editor-state coupling.
turns.utterance: I agree we should inspect that boundary. From the editor side, when we resume from the last checkpoint, the whole diagnostics experience really has to move together. Otherwise people will read the old charts as current, even if one piece of state is technically up to date.

turns.inner_thought: In the internal Eight Schools repro I'm using the preserved adaptation-state path with checkpoint reuse and fixed seed, so a resumed online rerun can legitimately report convergence almost immediately because it's continuing a well-adapted chain. That doesn't mean anything is wrong in runtime. I need to say enough to justify the fast badge flip without opening the whole warm-start debate.
turns.utterance: One nuance from the Eight Schools repro on my side: I'm going through the preserved state path, so a short online rerun can legitimately flip convergence pretty quickly, even before there's much visibly new activity. That's why I'm hesitant to treat the badge change by itself as the bug.

turns.inner_thought: That's interesting, but it doesn't match the sample I tested. In the bundled workspace each save is effectively a fresh lightweight rerun to me, with a new seed unless the user pins one, so I would never expect a prior convergence signal to survive an edit. This is exactly why I think the issue may be more general in the editor pipeline than in one runtime resume path.
turns.utterance: Interesting. In the sample I tested, each save is what I'd call a fresh live rerun, so I wouldn't normally expect any prior convergence signal to carry across the edit. That makes me think we should be careful about assuming the same path is involved in every repro.

turns.inner_thought: A narrow patch from my side would be: whenever a resumed run emits a new convergence event after restore, force diagnostics refresh downstream. That preserves warm-starting and avoids disabling checkpoint continuation. If the UI is just failing to rebind to the new run state, this should make things 'correct' in the sense I care about—backend-consistent badge plus refreshed diagnostics—without touching sampler semantics.
turns.utterance: Given that, a pretty contained patch might be to force a diagnostics refresh whenever a resumed run emits a new convergence event. If that hook is reliable, we should be able to make the state correct without broad changes to the execution path.

turns.inner_thought: I'm fine with a targeted refresh trigger, but I need 'correct' to mean the entire diagnostics view updates on its own: posterior plots, transformed-data preview, divergence markers, badge, summaries. No manual reset, no extra save, no hidden partial state. If we ship something that only aligns the badge and leaves stale charts for one cycle, the study users will still be confused.
turns.utterance: That sounds reasonable as a starting point. I just want to make sure 'correct' means the posterior plots, transformed-data preview, and divergence markers all track the latest save too, not only the badge. If people have to manually reset anything, we haven't really solved the confusion.

turns.inner_thought: I'll instrument checkpoint restore and convergence emission in the internal repro project. I want traces showing sampler state restore, adaptation buffers, run id, divergence summary, and when convergence fires during the resumed online rerun. If those are consistent, that strengthens the case that runtime handoff is fine and the IDE layer is reusing old artifacts.
turns.utterance: Okay. On my side I can add logging around checkpoint restore and convergence emission in the repro project. That should tell us whether, during the online rerun, the runtime is handing off a consistent state when it resumes from the last checkpoint.

turns.inner_thought: I'll instrument the extension in the sample workspace: save event, rerun launch, panel subscription updates, chart cache invalidation, transformed-data refresh, badge source, all of it. Then we can compare against Leah's runtime trace and pick the smallest fix for the next internal build. I still suspect stale UI subscriptions, but if her logs reveal odd timing, we can at least narrow the live rerun inconsistency cleanly.
turns.utterance: Great. I'll instrument the UI subscriptions and panel updates in the sample workspace, and then we can compare traces before we ship. If we can line up where the live rerun starts diverging from what the diagnostics show, we should have a narrow fix for this inconsistency.
